name: @sakaniui/mcp

tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Find SakaniUI components/blocks by what you need (e.g. "date picker", "sidebar navigation", "pricing"). Returns the best matches with import path, the release that added them and required props.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Full contract for one component or block: import path, the release that added it, every prop with type / allowed values / default / required, and the accessible-name rule. Use this before writing JSX.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List all components and blocks (name + one-line summary), optionally filtered by kind or category (e.g. Forms, Core, Marketing).

tools.name: get_tokens
tools.description: Design tokens (CSS custom properties). Pass a group (color, space, radius, shadow, font, motion, glass, surface, liquid, ...) and/or a substring to filter. Only these tokens exist.

tools.name: check_usage
tools.description: Validate props you are about to use against the contract: reports missing required props, values outside an enum, props that do not exist, and components the project's installed version does not have. Run it on each component you write.

props.description: prop name -> value (use true/false/numbers/strings; for non-literal values pass any placeholder)

tools.name: check_compatibility
tools.description: Compare the version this reference describes with the version installed in the project, and list what the project does not have yet. Call this first when you cannot tell which @sakaniui/react version the project uses (pass installedVersion, from `npm ls @sakaniui/react` or package.json).

tools.name: get_changelog
tools.description: Release notes that match a version. With `version`: that release. With `since`: every release after it, up to the version this reference describes. With neither: the releases between the project's installed version and this reference (or the latest release when they match or the project version is unknown).

tools.name: search_icons
tools.description: Find real icon names (Tabler set, exported from @sakaniui/react/icons) by meaning, e.g. "delete", "settings", "arrow right". Never guess an icon name: only names returned here exist.

tools.name: search_emoji
tools.description: Find real emoji component names (Fluent Emoji, exported from @sakaniui/react/emoji) by meaning, e.g. "rocket", "party", "thumbs up". Emoji are full colour and rendered as elements (<EmojiRocket />), not passed to icon props. Only names returned here exist.

tools.name: check_code
tools.description: Check a JSX/TSX snippet you wrote: imports from @sakaniui/react (and /blocks, /icons, /emoji) must exist, every SakaniUI element must have its required props, prop values must be allowed, and icon props must be real icon components passed as components. The code is only read, never run. Run it on every snippet before you answer.

code.description: The snippet, including its import lines.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: The AGENTS.md guide (principles, token rules, when nothing fits, glass, icons, per-component "why / when not to use", checklist). Pass a section number or heading text to get just that section; omit for the section list.

section.description: A section number ("3") or words from its heading ("icons").

instructions: SakaniUI 0.10.1. Read-only reference. Look components up with search_components / get_component and start from their `example`; find icon names with search_icons and emoji names with search_emoji (never guess them); search by the name you would normally use (dialog, snackbar, navbar, date picker) and it maps to the real component; run check_code on every snippet before you answer; style anything beyond props with the design tokens from get_tokens (CSS variables), not hard-coded colours or utility classes the project may not have; read get_guide when nothing fits. The project's installed @sakaniui/react version could not be detected, so this describes 0.10.1. Confirm it (npm ls @sakaniui/react) and call check_compatibility with installedVersion before suggesting a component.
